note: v2614: REG-593. His question was exactly right - has prune.arm proven itself to work already. Measured - EVERY axis in prune_wilson asserts a REFUSAL, _refused counts only the False arm, and replacing retention_may_act with a stub hardwired to always refuse scores IDENTICALLY - attempts 48 caught 48 either way. So 0.926 means it correctly says NO under 48 kinds of pressure and says NOTHING WHATEVER about the yes, while arming is exactly the act of trusting the yes. An invariant that always agrees may be perfect or INERT and those are indistinguishable until something proves the instrument can move. Added a BASELINE, not a sixth axis - it cannot raise the score, only withdraw it. With every precondition met the guard must PERMIT and say why; if it cannot, no claim may read PROVEN. AND THE FIRST CUT GATED ONLY THE PRINTED VERDICT - bank_into_proof_queue banked on attempts and caught alone and never read state, so a disowned run would still have written 48 of 48 into prune.arm and the lock would go on reading OPEN on evidence the harness had just withdrawn. Now the whole run refuses to bank. Verified the working path still banks all five claims, and that the baseline restores TV_AUTO_PRUNE even when the guard raises. Nothing here deletes - measured that importing control_app starts ZERO threads, _PRUNE_SAFE_TO_RUN is False, and the decider contains no remove or rmtree or unlink.
